title: Python SDK dataclass-first typed models & streaming response adapters
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Problem: Users building production services with the Python SDK need ergonomic, type-safe models for structured outputs, and consistent streaming adapters that integrate with typed response parsing. Current SDK helper patterns are fragmented: some example helpers use pydantic models, other internal helpers use ad-hoc dict parsing, and streaming endpoints return raw chunks that require manual assembly before validation. This causes runtime errors and poor DX when combining streaming, retries, and structured output contracts.

Goal: Implement a dataclass-first typed model layer (with optional pydantic compatibility) and a set of streaming response adapters that: (1) validate partial and final responses against typed schemas, (2) support both sync and async iteration ergonomics, (3) integrate with the SDK's retry/backoff logic without dropping partial state, and (4) include clear examples and migration notes for existing pydantic-based helpers. The work should improve developer ergonomics and reduce parsing-related incidents in production.

Scope:
- Introduce dataclass-based model definitions for common response types (GenerationResult, TokenDelta, ChoiceMetadata) with optional pydantic conversion helpers.
- Provide a StreamingResponseAdapter that yields validated model objects as tokens/frames arrive and raises structured validation errors on malformed payloads.
- Ensure adapters cooperate with SDK-level retries: on transient failures during a stream, adapters should offer a deterministic resume strategy (replay from last committed token or fallback to full-request retry) configurable per-route.
- Add sync/async iterator helpers matching Python idioms (for/async for, context manager support for resource cleanup).
- Ship example notebooks and snippets: small web server example that streams typed events to a client, a batch parser that consumes streaming output into typed objects, and migration snippets for existing pydantic-first users.
- Tests: unit tests for dataclass<->pydantic conversion, streaming edge cases (malformed frames, reconnects), retry integration tests that simulate partial response and resume.

Trade-offs considered:
- Pydantic-first vs dataclass-first: dataclasses are lighter-weight and integrate well with stdlib typing and serialization. We opt for dataclass-first with small pydantic wrappers for users who already rely on pydantic validators.
- Resume behavior: implementing an incremental resume requires protocol support from the server and subtle semantics. We'll provide a conservative default (no silent mid-stream state merge) and an opt-in resume policy for routes that support deterministic token offsets.
acceptance_criteria: Dataclass definitions for core response types exist and are documented
StreamingResponseAdapter provides both sync and async iteration and yields typed model instances
Adapters integrate with existing retry/backoff behavior and have a documented resume policy
Migration guide from pydantic-first helpers to dataclass-first examples is published
Unit and integration tests cover malformed frames, reconnect/resume scenarios, and pydantic conversion
Example demo (small Flask/Starlette app) shows streaming typed tokens to a client and is included in the SDK examples folder
comments: 2026-02-19 - Aisha Rao: Kickoff spike completed. Prototype dataclasses for GenerationResult and TokenDelta created. Benchmarks show negligible allocation overhead vs existing dict-based parsing for small payloads.

2026-02-25 - Marco Chen: Implemented StreamingResponseAdapter prototype (async iterator only). Pushing PR to get early feedback. Key open question: resume semantics when server returns overlapping token ranges. See PR for code comments.

2026-03-02 - Lena Ortiz (SDK PD): Reviewed prototype. Asked for sync iterator parity and context manager for deterministic cleanup. Also requested explicit examples showing how adapters behave under retry backoff.

2026-03-05 - Marco Chen: Added sync iterator wrapper and context manager. Began wiring adapter into SDK retry layer. Implemented test harness that simulates transient network errors and verifies adapter resume policy with 'abort' and 'replay' modes.

2026-03-10 - QA (Diego Martinez): Ran integration tests against staging inference service. Found edge case where partial frame with invalid JSON causes adapter to raise ValidationError instead of emitting a recoverable parse event. Marked as bug and added test. Assigned back to ENG-11420.

2026-03-12 - Marco Chen: Fixed partial-frame handling by introducing a streaming-framing buffer that defers validation until complete frame assembled. Updated PR and added tests for malformed frame handling. Ready for engineering review.
